title: SyncStatus.error and RestoreStatus.error carry a free-text message instead of a stable code, inviting raw/untranslated text downstream
why: EH-5 requires domain/data errors to carry stable codes/enums, never pre-formatted human messages, because this is an EN+Hebrew app where presentation must resolve text via AppLocalizations. Both status models instead expose a raw String message, and sync_providers.dart populates SyncStatus.error.message straight from error.toString() -- an unbounded, unlocalized, potentially technical string. This is not hypothetical: features/settings/presentation/widgets/backup_sync_section.dart already had to add an explicit guard (its own comment: 'never pass a raw exception string into the user-facing subtitle') to avoid rendering SyncStatusError.message directly, and lib/app/restore/device_restore_service.dart embeds RestoreStatus.error's message straight into a rethrown Exception's text. Any future consumer that pattern-matches .message without knowing about that workaround ships raw/English text to Hebrew-locale users.
recommendation: Replace the free-text message field on both SyncStatus.error and RestoreStatus.error with a stable enum/code (e.g. SyncErrorCode) plus optional non-user-facing debug detail, and have presentation resolve the code via AppLocalizations, per EH-5.
acceptance_criteria: EH-5 Rule-0 checker (grep for `required String message` on sealed status/result types, or raw error.toString() flowing into a domain model) passes.
backup_sync_section.dart's existing raw-string guard becomes structurally unnecessary because the type no longer exposes text to short-circuit around.

corrections: Finding's claim that device_restore_service.dart 'embeds RestoreStatus.error's message into a rethrown Exception' has causality reversed -- line 175 embeds SyncStatus.error's message into a thrown Exception, whose toString() then becomes RestoreStatus.error's message at line 252. Substance (unbounded raw text chaining through both models) still holds and is further confirmed by device_restore_screen.dart directly rendering it.

The 'why' text's claim that device_restore_service.dart 'embeds RestoreStatus.error's message straight into a rethrown Exception's text' is inaccurate — that behavior (embedding a .message field into a new thrown Exception) is exhibited by SyncStatusError at device_restore_service.dart:175, not RestoreStatus.error. RestoreStatus.error's message is only ever populated FROM e.toString() (device_restore_service.dart:252, restore_providers.dart:63), never read back into a new exception. Doesn't undermine the finding: independently found device_restore_screen.dart:219-220 renders RestoreStatus.error's raw .message directly in a Text widget with zero localization guard — stronger, directly-on-point evidence for the same P1 claim.
